The previous checksums were CARRIED OVER from younissk/lughaty packs/de and had never been reproduced here; they did not reproduce, and that was the correct result rather than a failure: those bytes came from a different repo's pipeline. method.frequency: ONE pass now. The old four-pass build existed because the treebank lemmatizer had to bootstrap off a surface ranking; Wikidata Lexemes is a standalone lexicon, so the table is complete before the first count is read. Every surface count is summed onto its LEMMA, and any key not attested in the corpora as a real surface form is dropped — that filter removed 85 entries that were 1990s spellings (kompromiß, paß) and lemmatizer artefacts (fachleut), and it is what keeps every published string traceable to CC BY Leipzig text.
method.lemmatizer: Wikidata Lexemes (CC0), German Q188, dump of 2026-07-29: 241,967 lexemes. Homographs resolved by corpus frequency of the candidate lemma. Three guards, each added after it caught a real error during the swap: a content-word POS guard (warten→warte, stärke→stärken), an affix-lexeme filter (in→-in deleted a top-20 word), and chain/cycle resolution to a fixpoint (das↔der was a mutual cycle that split the article paradigm at the head of the list). Adjective and participle endings are generated from known lemmas because Wikidata carries almost no German adjective declension — generated only where the corpus attests the form and it is not already a lemma of its own. ⚠️ A FOURTH GUARD was added while building Arabic, and it fixed German too: a RARITY check. A form is no longer mapped onto a lemma more than 200× rarer than itself. Without it the frequency tiebreak — which only compares candidates against each other, never against the form — produced heute→heuen (today→to make hay, 4,848×), kosten→kosen (to cost→to caress, 2,267×), fast→fasen (a lemma with ZERO corpus occurrences) and gilt→gelen. The threshold sits in a measured order-of-magnitude gap: correct mappings top out at 58.7× (eigenen→eigen), wrong ones start at 934×. It is also applied as a final sweep over the completed table, because adjective generation, hand-written overrides and chain resolution all add rows the candidate-level check never saw — which is exactly how fast→fasen survived the first version of the guard.
method.lemmatizerWarning: ⚠️ An earlier rule-based version produced silent, plausible errors: warten→waren (to wait→were), Ware→war, Seite→seit, Stärke→stark. Every one passed a both-words-are-common guard. A learner who proved `waren` would have been credited with `warten`. THE 2026-07-30 WIKIDATA SWAP REPRODUCED THIS CLASS THREE TIMES WITHIN AN HOUR, each in a new way — which is why the cases are now pinned as tests in builders/test_lemmas.py rather than relying on someone diffing the output.
method.filters: Surface forms shorter than 2 characters or outside the pack tokenize pattern are dropped. A form survives only if it appears in more than one corpus or at least 20 times, which removes the OCR and typo tail.
